Modularization One jar became many. / / part 1
The jar kept growing 2014 2025 Boot 1.0, the first release Boot 3.5. One big monolith, in every app. 185 KB → 2 MB / / spring-boot-autoconfigure.jar

Boot 4 split up its auto-configuration Boot 3.5 156 auto-configurations, all in this one jar / / spring-boot-autoconfigure.jar Boot 4.1 → 12 left in that jar. The rest moved into about 100 focused modules.

Jackson 3 The JSON library under everything. / / part 1

- What's new in the box / / jackson 3 + Immutable, builder-based configuration + Unchecked exceptions, better for lambdas and streams + Boot auto-configures a JsonMapper bean + ISO 8601 dates out of the box + New tools.jackson packages + Jackson 2 and 3 side by side

Inject the auto-configured mapper DataLoader.java @Component class DataLoader implements CommandLineRunner { private final JsonMapper mapper; private final ResourceLoader loader; DataLoader(JsonMapper mapper, ResourceLoader loader) { public void run(String } args) throws Exception { var json = loader.getResource(DONUTS_JSON).getInputStream(); donuts = mapper.readValue(json, new TypeReference<>() {}); } . . . ‌ . . . / } / / / jackson 3

What bites ! The databind packages moved to tools.jackson ! Mappers are immutable. Configure them with a builder. ! Dates are ISO 8601 strings, even in mappers you build ! A null for a primitive field now fails - / / jackson 3
spring.jackson.use-jackson2-defaults: true A bridge, not a home. It only covers Boot's own mapper. / / need more time?

Part 3 Small things, quietly useful null safety, BeanRegistrar, and six more
Null safety JSpecify, across the portfolio. / / part 3
Ever hit a NullPointerException? Yeah. Everyone. Every single one of you.
The problem isn't null. It's that nullness is implicit. Undocumented. The compiler can't help. / / the real problem

Four annotations, one standard / / jspecify.dev @Nullable @NonNull This value can be null. A field, return, parameter or generic. Null is never valid here. @NullMarked @NullUnmarked Everything in this scope is non-null by default. Nullness is unspecified. Opt a scope back out.

Spring's annotations go away package-info.java - @NonNullApi + @NullMarked package dev.danvega.talks; - import org.springframework.lang.NonNullApi; + import org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked; Talk.java - import org.springframework.lang.Nullable; / / + import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable; / / / / delete: org.springframework.lang −4 annotations

Spring's annotations go away package-info.java + @NullMarked package dev.danvega.talks; + import org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked; Talk.java / / + import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable; / / / / delete: org.springframework.lang −4 annotations

BeanRegistrar @Import(Feeds.class) on any @Configuration class Feeds implements BeanRegistrar { public void register(BeanRegistry registry, Environment env) { for (String name : List.of("devoxx", "jfall")) { registry.registerBean(name + "Feed", Feed.class, spec -> spec.supplier(ctx -> new Feed(name))); } if (env.matchesProfiles("dev")) { registry.registerBean("mirror", Mirror.class, spec -> spec.lazyInit() .supplier(ctx -> new Mirror(ctx.bean("jfallFeed", Feed.class)))); } } ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ / } / / / framework 7
